subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting remain Gateway-internal after memory watcher fixes are validated, or should OpenClaw add a restart-aware or out-of-process lifecycle signal for stuck cron jobs?
rationale: The source shows useful restart accounting, but the issue's central silent-failure concern is that the same Gateway process may be too starved to deliver failureAlert before restart; that tradeoff needs product ownership rather than an automatic patch.

options.title: Validate current main first
options.body: Run a macOS launchd soak on current main or the latest release with the reported memory/QMD corpus and cron cluster, then choose alert architecture only if silent failure remains.

options.title: Treat memory fixes as sufficient
options.body: Close only after soak proof shows heap/RSS growth and silent cron failures no longer reproduce without adding a new alert path.

options.title: Add independent cron lifecycle signaling
options.body: Design a restart-aware or out-of-process started/succeeded/stuck signal so alerting is not blocked by the same wedged Gateway process.

recommendation.title: Validate current main first
recommendation.body: Run a macOS launchd soak on current main or the latest release with the reported memory/QMD corpus and cron cluster, then choose alert architecture only if silent failure remains.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current implementation overlap is the merged memory-core watcher fix, and that owner can help validate whether residual memory pressure remains before cron alert architecture changes are chosen.
